blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

img.alt: Diagram showing how hydro jetting clears a residential sewer line, with a cross-section view of the underground pipe, jet nozzle, high-pressure water spray, and debris being flushed toward the street connection

blocks.h2: When Elgin Homes Need Hydro Jetting

tiles.body: The line clears, then clogs again in a few months. The pipe walls are still coated.

tiles.h3: Grease Has Built Up in the Kitchen Line
tiles.body: Grease hardens in layers. Jetting removes them instead of punching a hole.
Jetting strips decades of rust scale so the pipe carries its full volume again.
A liner bonds to clean pipe. Jetting is the first step of every lining job.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting and Elgin's Older Lines
blocks.intro: About 1 in 5 Elgin homes was built before 1940. Lines that old carry a lot of history inside them.

items.body: In east side clay lines, rodding cuts the main root mass but leaves fine roots at the joints. Jetting clears them so the line stays open longer.

items.h3: Kitchen Lines in Updated Older Homes
items.body: A kitchen remodel doesn't replace the old drain behind the wall. Years of grease in that original line are a common jetting job.
Large families in newer homes send a lot of grease and soap down the drain. Jetting resets lines that have narrowed over 20 or 30 years.
We confirm the pipe can handle the pressure first, then show you the clean line when we're done.

steps.body: We camera the line for breaks or a collapse. Jetting a broken pipe can make it worse.
We clean the full line and set the pressure for clay, cast iron or PVC.
A second camera pass shows the result. You get the price before any of it starts.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: Is hydro jetting better than rodding?
items.preview: For buildup and returning roots, yes. For a simple clog, rodding is enough.
items.answer: For a simple clog, rodding is fast and effective. For grease, scale or roots that keep coming back, jetting cleans the whole pipe wall and lasts longer.

items.q: Can jetting damage an old pipe?
items.preview: Not a sound one. We camera it first to be sure.
items.answer: Not a pipe that's in good condition. We inspect it on camera and set the pressure for the material. If a section is broken, we'll recommend a [repair](/elgin/sewer-repair) first.

items.q: How long does a jetting job take?
items.preview: Usually a few hours, including the camera passes.
items.answer: Most residential jobs take a few hours, including the camera inspection before and after.

items.q: Will jetting stop roots from coming back?
items.preview: It slows them down. Lining stops them.
items.answer: Jetting clears roots more completely than rodding, so they take longer to return. To stop them for good, the joints have to be sealed with a [trenchless liner](/elgin/trenchless-sewer-repair) or replaced.

items.q: How much does hydro jetting cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the line and buildup. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the length of the line, access and how much buildup there is. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
